body.statement: On every primitive stratum defined by \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\mbox{-}system}\), each active cell's complete-event conditional envelope \(M_j\) and the global envelope \(F\) are finite maxima and minima of analytic or Puiseux-continuable branches. The global maximizing holdout set consists exactly of the retained interval endpoints, projected branch endpoints, stationary branch roots, branch intersections, and flat maximizing intervals attaining \(V^{\star}\); for each such \(\rho\), the full weight set is \(\prod_{j=(C,s)\in J}\{\theta_j:\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge V^{\star}\}\). This characterization is necessary and sufficient in all positive, negative, zero, and mixed-sign \(\Delta\) regimes, with every \(\Pi_j\) conditioned on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\).
body.proof_tex:
The residual-scale bound places \(\lvert r_j\rvert\) uniformly below one. The bivariate Gaussian upper tail is real analytic in its two thresholds and correlation on this compact positive-definite domain. Its derivative with respect to the critical threshold is a strictly negative Gaussian density. The analytic implicit-function theorem therefore makes \(q_{\alpha,j}\), and hence \(p_j(\rho,\theta)=\Pi_j(\rho,\theta,\ell_s)\), real analytic on a neighborhood of \(I\times[0,\pi/2]\).

Let \(A_j=\partial_\theta p_j\). The derivative formula in the weight-side proof gives \(A_j(\rho,0)=b_{2j}\ell_sD_{\ell_s}>0\), so \(A_j\) is not identically zero on any two-dimensional open set. Its zero set on the compact rectangle is semianalytic of dimension at most one. The finite semianalytic-stratification theorem decomposes it into finitely many analytic arcs and points. Splitting arcs at critical values of projection onto \(\rho\), at multiple roots, and at the rectangle boundary produces finitely many graphs \(\theta_{j\ell}(\rho)\) on open subintervals. At their endpoints the local Weierstrass polynomial supplies the finite ramified continuation used by the branch system; persistent repeated factors are reduced and retained rather than discarded.

For a fixed \(\rho\), a maximum in \(\theta\) occurs at an angular endpoint or at one of these stationary graphs. Consequently
\[
M_j(\rho)=\max_\ell g_{j\ell}(\rho),\qquad
g_{j\ell}(\rho)=p_j\{\rho,\theta_{j\ell}(\rho)\},\qquad
F(\rho)=\min_jM_j(\rho),
\]
with angular endpoints included as branches. Refine the finite interval decomposition at all nonidentical branch crossings, nontransverse crossings, and projected arc endpoints. On every remaining interval the ordering of all branches and cells is fixed, so \(F\) equals one analytic branch. Such a branch attains an interior maximum only at a stationary root unless it is constant; a constant branch contributes its entire flat interval. Adding both endpoints of \(I\), all projected branch endpoints, all stationary roots, all branch intersections, and all flat intervals is therefore exhaustive and necessary. Multiple-root, tie, and identical-branch predicates are exactly those retained by the branch system, so no genericity or exact numerical equality decision has been imposed. The argument is independent of the signs of the \(\Delta_j\); the weight-side and endpoint theorems merely prune candidates on their respective strata.

It remains to recover all weights. Independence of the cell-specific angles gives, for fixed \(\rho\),
\[
\max_{(\theta_j)}\min_jp_j(\rho,\theta_j)=\min_j\max_{\theta_j}p_j(\rho,\theta_j)=F(\rho).
\]
The first inequality in each direction follows respectively by choosing every cellwise maximizer and by bounding each \(p_j\) by \(M_j\). Thus a design attains \(V^\star\) if and only if its holdout is in the exhaustive maximizing set just described and every coordinate satisfies \(p_j(\rho,\theta_j)\ge V^\star\). This is precisely the displayed product of full superlevel sets, including all slack-cell continua, and proves necessity and sufficiency.
body.justification: This supplies the complete mixed-sign analytic geometry and preserves all ties and slack-cell weight continua.
body.gap: Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu optimize a discretized policy program and do not characterize the continuous holdout argmax correspondence or its equality strata.
body.consumer: The complete candidate list supports auditable global design optimization even when the optimizer is nonunique or lies on a branch transition.
